title: Set Point Theory: Why Your Body Resists Weight Loss

authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: Why does the body seem to resist and reverse weight loss, and what is 'set point theory'?
reader_intent: Understand the biological basis for weight-loss resistance and regain to reduce self-blame.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader understands adaptive thermogenesis and set point theory as real biological phenomena, with accurate scope on what is and isn't known, rather than an overclaimed specific number.

claims.proposition: The body's set point is not a fixed number but a range, typically spanning about 10-15 pounds.
claims.article_location: "What Is Set Point Theory?" section, second paragraph
claims.recommended_action: This is the exact kind of pseudo-citation Issue #16 warned against: a specific numeric range with zero source capable of supporting it (the article's own Sources list is five generic organization homepages — NIH, Endocrine Society, APA, NIDDK, Obesity Society — none of which is cited as specifically supporting this number). Either locate and cite a primary source stating this specific range, or generalize the claim to avoid asserting an unsupported number.

claims.proposition: Adaptive thermogenesis (metabolic adaptation) after weight loss involves decreased resting metabolic rate, increased ghrelin/decreased leptin, decreased NEAT, and improved muscle efficiency.
claims.recommended_action: Directionally consistent with claim-biggestloser-rmr-below-baseline and claim-biggestloser-metabolic-adaptation-residual, though the article does not cite Fothergill et al. by name or number. Recommend citing that source directly and carrying its specific n=14/atypical-cohort limitation forward rather than presenting adaptive thermogenesis as a fully generalized phenomenon.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Reader learning about adaptive thermogenesis benefits from the broader metabolism-myths context.
Set point theory builds directly on the leptin/ghrelin mechanisms explained there.

disposition_reason: One of the highest-value findings in this audit: a specific, unsupported numeric claim (the 10-15 lb 'defended weight range') is stated as fact with no source capable of supporting it, despite the article otherwise being a genuinely valuable, well-hedged explanation of a real phenomenon. Cannot be KEEP while this claim is unresolved. The broader adaptive-thermogenesis content can be strengthened by directly citing the corpus's own Fothergill-based claims.
blocking_findings: Specific 'defended weight range of 10-15 pounds' claim has no supporting source and must be sourced or generalized before this article can be reconsidered for KEEP.
required_research: Locate a primary source (if one exists) for the specific 10-15 lb defended-range figure, or rewrite the claim to avoid an unsupported specific number.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Directly cite claim-biggestloser-rmr-below-baseline / claim-biggestloser-metabolic-adaptation-residual and carry forward their n=14/atypical-cohort limitations rather than generalizing adaptive thermogenesis without qualification.
safety_language_findings: Appropriately frames set-point biology as real but not deterministic; no guaranteed-outcome language.
Correctly avoids implying every individual has an identical, precisely-known set point.
